response.sql: WITH m AS (SELECT o.mktnote, f.feerate - f.rebrate AS net FROM fees f JOIN orders o ON o.recordvault = f.orderslink), g AS (SELECT mktnote, AVG(net) AS a FROM m GROUP BY mktnote), b AS (SELECT AVG(net) AS bm FROM m) SELECT AVG(g.a) AS avg_of_pair_avg_net_rate, AVG(g.a - b.bm) AS avg_excess_over_benchmark FROM g CROSS JOIN b WHERE g.a > b.bm

assumptions.assumption: orders.recordvault is unique, as documented, so each fee record matches at most one order and the join does not duplicate fee records.
A fee record with a NULL feerate or rebrate has a NULL net rate. It is skipped in the averages instead of having the NULL treated as 0.
Fee records whose order has a NULL mktnote form a single group, which GROUP BY does by default.
